title: Tune evolution
summary: Decide how the next generation is made: species, parents, mutation and champions.

steps.title: Species protect new ideas
steps.body:
NEAT, the method that trains these brains, groups similar brains into species. A brain mostly competes with its own species.

That matters because a new idea usually starts out worse. A brain that just grew a new neuron has not tuned it yet. Inside its own species it gets a few generations to improve before it has to beat the leaders.

`speciate(target: 8)` aims for about 8 species. More species keep more variety alive, fewer focus on the best ideas so far.
hints: speciate takes one setting, target, the number of species to aim for.

steps.title: Choose the parents
steps.body:
Only the best part of each species gets to have children. `select(top: 20%)` lets the top fifth breed.

A small share pushes hard toward what works today. A large share keeps more variety, which helps when today's leaders are heading for a dead end. Machine learning people call this the balance between exploitation and exploration.
hints: select takes one setting, top, the share of each species that may breed.

steps.title: Mutation is exploration
steps.body:
A child mixes two parents (crossover) and then changes a little at random (mutation). Mutation nudges weights, and now and then adds a connection or a whole neuron so the brain can grow.

The starter sets every mutation chance to 0. Press Check: children can only remix brains that already exist, so progress stalls after a few generations.

Turn mutation back on with the usual chances: weights 0.8, addConnection 0.05, addNode 0.03 and toggle 0.01.

check.message: Training should get the best car past 300 m on the Hairpin.

hints: Each number inside mutate is a chance between 0 and 1.
Use mutate: { weights: 0.8, addConnection: 0.05, addNode: 0.03, toggle: 0.01 }.

steps.title: Never lose the best
steps.body:
Mutation can break a good brain as easily as it improves one. `keepChampions()` copies the best brain of each species into the next generation unchanged, so the best result so far never gets worse.

It is already on by default, which is why the editor says it uses its default setting. Write it out anyway: a script that says what it does is easier to read, and the last warning goes away.

check.message: The script should compile with no warnings.

hints: The call takes no settings at all.
